Gelatinous Guardian Quirk.name: Gelatinous Guardian Quirk
Gelatinous Guardian Quirk.description:
🫧 You produce living medicinal slime and have a partly gel body, combining your doctor father's healing with your mother's liquid manipulation.

🌱 Start by softening blunt hits, squeezing gaps, cushioning short falls and sealing bleeding or cooling burns with gel. Healing is real and slow.
📈 Training adds sticky capture, sealed doors, injured transport and larger fall cushions. Only your own noncorrosive gel answers you.
⚠️ Heat, drying and sharp edges threaten gel; it cannot regrow limbs or replace blood. Common drawback pairing: Stamina Drain, from production and healing.
⚖️ Seek patient consent where possible; restraint needs self-defense or licensed duty. Gel protects wounds and speeds recovery while hospital care remains necessary.
🎬 Similar canon Quirks: Recovery Girl (Heal); Mina Ashido (Acid), for material feel only.

📈 Grants: Endurance +1, Quirk Control +10, Quirk Stamina +10, First Aid +5
⚡ Starting techniques: Medicinal Wrap, Yielding Guard
Gelatinous Guardian Quirk.traitNarrativeEffects: Scale: living medicinal gel in skin and tissue, oozed from the hands. New adult user: about a bucket of own gel within 3 m; pads a low fall, seals an arm wound, slips shoulder-width gaps. Limits: own gel only; organs in a weak torso core; no splitting or phasing; eases blunt hits, not blades or bullets; heat dries, cold stiffens; dirty gel cannot heal. Healing (sustained touch) seals bleeding, speeds repair in minutes-hours; never replaces blood, regrows limbs, cures all or revives. Loose gel stops beyond range, dries in an hour. Quirk Strain: light: wrap, guard; moderate: sticky capture, squeeze, cooling; heavy: patient carry, fall cushion; severe: rescue spread, long dressings, awakened uses. Fusion: father's healing + mother's liquid manipulation. Type: Mutant (also fits Emitter). Law: consent if possible; restraint beyond self-defense or duty: unlawful confinement. Tagline: "I'm not a bad slime!" Look: translucent gel.
